clue.text: Admission made by expert going round cape by ship

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
SS stands for steamship, placed beside the rest

explanation.surface: A sailor-expert gains entry by rounding a headland on a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cape' suggests a garment or headland scene, but it is just the map abbreviation; 'by ship' means the steamship letters follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Access is the right of entry, which is what admission grants.

clue.text: Animal, for instance, found on top of Snowdon

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above what follows
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the mountain

explanation.surface: A creature, say a goat, spotted on the summit of Wales's highest peak.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a donkey, a kind of animal.

clue.text: Head of company, young woman in charge of major sporting event

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A firm's chief and a young woman run a big tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Classics are the major horse races in Britain, and any great sporting fixture can be called a classic.

clue.text: Storage time of product if kept by the Parisian under bar

indicators.note: in a down entry, under places one piece below another

parts.note: a shelf is a ledge or bar

indicators.note: something kept by another is held inside it

explanation.surface: How long a product lasts if a Frenchman stores it under the pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but here it is a ledge; in a down entry 'under' puts the rest below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelf life is the period a product can be stored before it spoils.

clue.text: Sound off, say, on strike

parts.note: to say something is to speak

explanation.surface: A striking worker voices complaints loudly on the picket line.
explanation.definitionFit: To sound off is an idiom for voicing an opinion forcefully, as does speaking out.

clue.text: Propose issue carries soft drinks article

indicators.note: in a down entry a word that carries others holds them up, so they sit above it

parts.note: an issue is a question under discussion

explanation.surface: A proposal on the subject of soft drinks is put forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop the question is an idiom for making a proposal of marriage.

clue.text: Runs in a boy responsible for crime

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A lad who ran off was to blame for an offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a crime.

clue.text: Actor, one in Bart musical!

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A performer cast in a Lionel Bart show.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside OLIVER; the exclamation mark echoes the musical's title, Oliver!
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was one of the most celebrated English stage and film actors.

clue.text: Really get at awfully old place for viewing art

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone truly attacks a dreadful old exhibition hall.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tate Gallery in London was renamed Tate Britain in 2000, hence an old name for an art museum.

clue.text: Carnegie, say, identified by philosophy this patron exercised

parts.note: Phil is the abbreviation for philosophy

indicators.note: exercised means worked or put through movements, so the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: The industrialist Carnegie is known for a sponsor's worked-out philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Carnegie gave away most of his fortune, a classic example of a charitable benefactor.

clue.text: Chips and peas cooked in craft

indicators.note: food that is cooked is altered and mixed, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A meal of chips and peas prepared aboard a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like cooking skill, but it means a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A craft is any vessel, and a spaceship is a vessel for travelling through space.

clue.text: Riddle involving western satirist

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one word holds another

parts.note: to riddle is to sieve, or sift
W is the abbreviation for western

explanation.surface: A puzzle concerning a cowboy writer who mocks society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' suggests a puzzle, but here it is a verb: a riddle is also a coarse sieve. W sits inside SIFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift, author of Gulliver's Travels and A Modest Proposal, is a famous satirist.

clue.text: Fun whilst hiking? That could be an over-optimistic expectation

indicators.note: saying letters could be something invites rearranging them into it

explanation.surface: Expecting a walk in the hills to be enjoyable may be too hopeful.
explanation.definitionFit: Wishful thinking is belief based on what one hopes for rather than on the facts.

clue.text: Readily sympathetic, armed with wreath, possibly

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters may form something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: Bringing flowers to a funeral shows a kind heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm-hearted person is kind and quick to feel compassion for others.

clue.text: Uproar in court needs sorting out

indicators.note: something that needs sorting out is in disorder, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A judge must restore order after a disturbance in the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as a link, but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruction is a noisy disturbance or row, the same as an uproar.

clue.text: Small pane of glass, cause of dispute

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small diamond-shaped pane used in leaded windows
second meaning: a reason for complaint, as in having no argument with someone

explanation.surface: A broken little window pane starts a row between neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: The glazing sense is rare: a quarrel (or quarry) is a diamond pane in a leaded window.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a glazier's diamond pane and a grievance one has with somebody.

clue.text: Boy appears in a doorway with whole amount

indicators.note: appearing in something means standing within it

explanation.surface: A lad turns up at the entrance carrying everything.
explanation.walkthrough: GREG goes inside A GATE, after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggregate is a total formed by adding everything together.

clue.text: Half of rugby team seen in front of church in North Wales town

indicators.note: being in front puts one piece directly before the next
taking half of a name means keeping its first part and dropping the rest

parts.note: Harlequins is a London rugby union club
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Rugby players are spotted outside a chapel in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: Harlequins is a London rugby union club with a ten-letter name, so half of it is its first five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlech is a small town in Gwynedd, north-west Wales, known for its castle.

clue.text: Seeks information about eastern joints

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round another

parts.note: to refer to a book is to consult it for information
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: Someone asks about oriental cannabis cigarettes.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside REFERS after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is slang for a cannabis cigarette, which is also called a joint.

clue.text: Warning posted in sunken garden

indicators.note: something posted in a place is stationed inside it, so look within the next words

explanation.surface: A notice put up in a recessed garden.
explanation.definitionFit: En garde is the call a fencer gives to warn an opponent to take guard.

clue.text: Studying for an English university place

definitions.meaning: first meaning: studying a subject, as at university
second meaning: a Berkshire town with its own university

explanation.surface: A student is preparing to apply to an English university.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject is British for studying it, and Reading is a town in Berkshire with a university.

clue.text: Medical treatment of a type they criticise inside

indicators.note: inside places one word within another word

parts.note: a type or variant is a version
to rap is to criticise sharply

explanation.surface: Some form of medicine that its practitioners themselves condemn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criticise inside' reads as a description of the treatment but is a container instruction acting on 'they'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aversion therapy is a psychiatric treatment pairing an unwanted habit with unpleasant stimuli.

clue.text: Walk off with pirate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to take something without permission
second meaning: as a verb, to copy or take another's goods illegally

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pirate' reads as a noun, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe theft: making off with property and plundering it unlawfully.

clue.text: Article attracting touching expression of sympathy

indicators.note: attracting draws one thing to sit beside another

parts.note: re means concerning, or touching on

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece draws heartfelt comments of compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' looks like the sentimental adjective, but it means 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'There, there' is a soothing word said to comfort someone upset.

clue.text: Sail on it at sea admitting love of solitude

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so another letter goes inside
at sea means confused and adrift, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A lone sailor relishes being alone on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters ISLATION take O after their second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolation is the state of being alone, which is what solitude means.

clue.text: Number on the way up for final

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: A figure climbing towards a last result.
explanation.definitionFit: A net amount is the final figure left after all deductions.

clue.text: Lose backing during meeting? That's extremely sad

indicators.note: something during an event happens within it, so it sits inside

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is read in the other direction

explanation.surface: Losing support at a gathering leaves someone very unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meeting' means a romantic or social appointment here, and 'backing' acts on 'Lose' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate describes someone overwhelmed with grief or misery.

clue.text: Reportedly delay mass

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is told by word of mouth, so go by sound

explanation.surface: A church service is said to be postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' tempts as the church service, but it is the physical quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: In everyday use weight and mass both mean how heavy something is.
